terms.gloss: you're making fun of me, you're kidding
terms.grammar: lūdō with the person as object: “you are playing with me”
evidence: Hor. S. 2.5.58: an prūdēns lūdis mē obscūra canendō? (Lewis & Short), s.v. furō

terms.grammar: nē with the present subjunctive, a prohibition

sources: Lewis & Short: ludo · Lewis & Short: jocor
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 101, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
